obligations.quote: For each instance an incarcerated person is placed in de-escalation confinement as described in subdivision c of this section, the department shall prepare an incident report that includes a detailed description of why isolation was necessary to de-escalate an immediate conflict and the length of time the incarcerated person was placed in such confinement.
obligations.law_title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to banning solitary confinement in city jails and establishing standards for the use of restrictive housing and emergency lock-ins

obligations.action_summary: Provide the speaker of the council and the board of correction all de-escalation confinement incident reports for the preceding quarter and post such reports on the department's website with personally identifying information redacted.
obligations.quote: Beginning on July 15, 2024, and within 15 days of the end of each subsequent quarter, the department shall provide the speaker of the council and the board of correction all such reports for the preceding quarter and post all such reports on the department's website. The department shall redact all personally identifying information prior to posting such reports on the department's website.
obligations.deadline_text: Beginning on July 15, 2024, and within 15 days of the end of each subsequent quarter
obligations.law_title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to banning solitary confinement in city jails and establishing standards for the use of restrictive housing and emergency lock-ins

obligations.action_summary: Provide the speaker of the council and the board of correction a quarterly report on de-escalation confinement data disaggregated by race, age, gender identity, mental health treatment level, and duration, and post on the department's website.
obligations.quote: Beginning July 31, 2024, and within 30 days of the end of each subsequent quarter, the department shall provide to the speaker of the council and the board of correction, and post on the department's website, a report with data for the preceding quarter on the total number of people placed in such confinement, disaggregated by race, age, gender identity and mental health treatment level, as well as the total number of people held in such confinement disaggregated by whether confinement lasted less than one hour, between one and two hours, between two and three hours, and between three and four hours.
obligations.deadline_text: Beginning July 31, 2024, and within 30 days of the end of each subsequent quarter
obligations.law_title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to banning solitary confinement in city jails and establishing standards for the use of restrictive housing and emergency lock-ins

obligations.action_summary: Refrain from placing incarcerated persons in restraints unless an individualized determination is made that restraints are necessary to prevent imminent risk of self-injury or injury, using only the least restrictive form for no longer than necessary.
obligations.quote: The department shall not place an incarcerated person in restraints unless an individualized determination is made that restraints are necessary to prevent an imminent risk of self-injury or injury to other persons. In such instances, only the least restrictive form of restraints may be used and may be used no longer than is necessary to abate such imminent harm.
obligations.law_title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to banning solitary confinement in city jails and establishing standards for the use of restrictive housing and emergency lock-ins

obligations.action_summary: Refrain from using restraints on incarcerated persons under age 22 except during transportation or escorted movement within a facility when an individualized determination is made that restraints are necessary to prevent imminent risk of self-injury or injury.
obligations.quote: Restraints shall not be used on an incarcerated person under the age of 22 except in the following circumstances: (i) during transportation in and out of a facility, provided that during transportation no person shall be secured to an immovable object; and (ii) during escorted movement within a facility to and from out-of-cell activities where an individualized determination is made that restraints are necessary to prevent an immediate risk of self-injury or injury to other persons.
obligations.law_title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to banning solitary confinement in city jails and establishing standards for the use of restrictive housing and emergency lock-ins

obligations.action_summary: Refrain from engaging in attempts to unnecessarily prolong, delay, or undermine an individual's escorted movements.
obligations.quote: The department is prohibited from engaging in attempts to unnecessarily prolong, delay or undermine an individual's escorted movements.
obligations.law_title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to banning solitary confinement in city jails and establishing standards for the use of restrictive housing and emergency lock-ins

obligations.action_summary: Hold a hearing to determine if continued use of restraints is necessary before placing an incarcerated person in restraints beyond initial use or on two consecutive days.
obligations.quote: The department shall not place an incarcerated person in restraints beyond the use of restraints described in paragraph 1 of this subdivision, or on two consecutive days, until a hearing is held to determine if the continued use of restraints is necessary for the safety of others.
obligations.law_title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to banning solitary confinement in city jails and establishing standards for the use of restrictive housing and emergency lock-ins

obligations.action_summary: Review continued use of restraints on a daily basis and discontinue once there is no longer an imminent risk of self-injury or injury, with continued use authorized for no more than seven consecutive days.
obligations.quote: Any continued use of restraints must be reviewed by the department on a daily basis and discontinued once there is no longer an imminent risk of self-injury or injury to other persons. Continued use of restraints may only be authorized for seven consecutive days.
obligations.law_title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to banning solitary confinement in city jails and establishing standards for the use of restrictive housing and emergency lock-ins

obligations.action_summary: Refrain from placing an incarcerated person in restrictive housing until a hearing is held and the person is found to have committed a violent grade I offense.
obligations.quote: Except as provided in subdivision g of this section, the department shall not place an incarcerated person in restrictive housing until a hearing on such placement is held and the person is found to have committed a violent grade I offense.
obligations.law_title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to banning solitary confinement in city jails and establishing standards for the use of restrictive housing and emergency lock-ins

obligations.action_summary: Establish rules for restrictive housing hearings including representation rights, right to present evidence and cross-examine witnesses, witness requirements, notice provisions, and hearing disposition standards.
obligations.quote: The board of correction shall establish rules for restrictive housing hearings that shall, at a minimum, include the following provisions
obligations.deadline_text: before such date
obligations.law_title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to banning solitary confinement in city jails and establishing standards for the use of restrictive housing and emergency lock-ins

obligations.action_summary: Provide incarcerated persons and their legal counsel or advocate written notice of reasons for proposed restrictive housing placement and supporting evidence no later than 48 hours prior to the restrictive housing hearing.
obligations.quote: The department shall provide the incarcerated person and their legal counsel or advocate written notice of the reason for proposed placement in restrictive housing and any supporting evidence for such placement, no later than 48 hours prior to the restrictive housing hearing
obligations.deadline_text: no later than 48 hours prior to the restrictive housing hearing
obligations.law_title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to banning solitary confinement in city jails and establishing standards for the use of restrictive housing and emergency lock-ins

obligations.action_summary: Provide legal counsel or advocate adequate time to prepare for restrictive housing hearings and grant reasonable requests for adjournments.
obligations.quote: The department shall provide the legal counsel or advocate adequate time to prepare for such hearings and shall grant reasonable requests for adjournments
obligations.law_title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to banning solitary confinement in city jails and establishing standards for the use of restrictive housing and emergency lock-ins

obligations.action_summary: Take reasonable steps to provide incarcerated persons an interpreter in their native language if they do not understand or are unable to communicate in English at restrictive housing hearings.
obligations.quote: An incarcerated person shall have the right to an interpreter in their native language if the person does not understand or is unable to communicate in English. The department shall take reasonable steps to provide such interpreter
obligations.law_title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to banning solitary confinement in city jails and establishing standards for the use of restrictive housing and emergency lock-ins

obligations.action_summary: Videotape any refusal by an incarcerated person to attend restrictive housing hearings and include the videotape in the hearing record.
obligations.quote: A refusal by an incarcerated person to attend any restrictive housing hearings must be videotaped and made part of the hearing record
obligations.law_title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to banning solitary confinement in city jails and establishing standards for the use of restrictive housing and emergency lock-ins

obligations.action_summary: Document in writing the basis for excluding or removing an incarcerated person from a restrictive housing hearing if exclusion/removal is determined necessary to prevent jeopardy to safety or facility security.
obligations.quote: If the incarcerated person is excluded or removed from a restrictive housing hearing because it is determined that such person's presence will jeopardize the safety of themselves or others or security of the facility, the basis for such exclusion must be documented in the hearing record
obligations.law_title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to banning solitary confinement in city jails and establishing standards for the use of restrictive housing and emergency lock-ins

obligations.action_summary: Reach a restrictive housing disposition within five business days after hearing conclusion, supported by substantial evidence in writing with detailed information on findings, witness testimony, evidence relied upon, and sanction imposed.
obligations.quote: A restrictive housing disposition shall be reached within five business days after the conclusion of the hearing. Such disposition must be supported by substantial evidence, shall be documented in writing, and must contain the following information: a finding of guilty or not guilty, a summary of each witness's testimony and whether their testimony was credited or rejected with the reasons thereof, the evidence relied upon by the hearing officer in reaching their finding, and the sanction imposed, if any
obligations.deadline_text: within five business days after the conclusion of the hearing
obligations.law_title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to banning solitary confinement in city jails and establishing standards for the use of restrictive housing and emergency lock-ins

obligations.action_summary: Provide incarcerated persons and their counsel or advocate a written copy of the restrictive housing hearing disposition within 24 hours of determination.
obligations.quote: A written copy of the hearing disposition shall be provided to the incarcerated person and their counsel or advocate within 24 hours of the determination.
obligations.deadline_text: within 24 hours of the determination
obligations.law_title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to banning solitary confinement in city jails and establishing standards for the use of restrictive housing and emergency lock-ins

obligations.action_summary: Prepare incident reports for each instance a disciplinary charge resulting in restrictive housing is dismissed or an incarcerated person is found not guilty, including description of the charge and reasons for dismissal or not guilty determination.
obligations.quote: For each instance a disciplinary charge that could result in restrictive housing is dismissed or an incarcerated individual is found not guilty of the disciplinary charge, the department shall prepare an incident report that includes a description of the disciplinary charge and the reasons for the dismissal or not guilty determination.
obligations.law_title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to banning solitary confinement in city jails and establishing standards for the use of restrictive housing and emergency lock-ins

obligations.action_summary: Prepare incident reports for each instance an incarcerated person is placed in restrictive housing, including detailed description of behavior resulting in placement and why restrictive housing was necessary.
obligations.quote: For each instance an incarcerated person is placed in restrictive housing, the department shall prepare an incident report that includes a detailed description of the behavior that resulted in placement in restrictive housing and why restrictive housing was necessary to address such behavior, including if a person was placed in pre-hearing temporary restrictive housing and the reasons why the situation met the requirements in paragraph 1 of subdivision g of this section.
obligations.law_title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to banning solitary confinement in city jails and establishing standards for the use of restrictive housing and emergency lock-ins

obligations.action_summary: Prepare incident reports for each instance restrictive housing confinement continues after a 15-day review, including description of how the person continued to present a specific, significant and imminent threat and what program, treatment, service, or corrective action was required before discharge.
obligations.quote: For each instance in which confinement in restrictive housing is continued after a 15-day review of an incarcerated person's placement in restrictive housing, the department shall prepare an incident report as to why the person was not discharged, including a detailed description of how the person continued to present a specific, significant and imminent threat to the safety and security of the facility if housed outside restrictive housing and what program, treatment, service, and/or corrective action was required before discharge.
obligations.law_title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to banning solitary confinement in city jails and establishing standards for the use of restrictive housing and emergency lock-ins

obligations.action_summary: Provide the speaker of the council and the board of correction all restrictive housing incident reports for the preceding quarter and post such reports on the department's website with personally identifying information redacted.
obligations.quote: Beginning on July 15, 2024, and within 15 days of the end of each subsequent quarter, the department shall provide the speaker of the council and the board of correction all such reports for the prior quarter and post all such reports on the department's website. The department shall redact all personally identifying information prior to posting the reports on the department's website.
obligations.deadline_text: Beginning on July 15, 2024, and within 15 days of the end of each subsequent quarter
obligations.law_title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to banning solitary confinement in city jails and establishing standards for the use of restrictive housing and emergency lock-ins

obligations.action_summary: Provide the speaker of the council and the board of correction a quarterly report on restrictive housing data including total number of people placed, disaggregated by race, age, gender identity, mental health treatment level, length of time, and disposition outcomes, and post on the department's website.
obligations.quote: Beginning July 31, 2024, and within 30 days of the end of each subsequent quarter, the department shall provide to the speaker of the council and the board of correction, and post on the department's website, a report with data for the preceding quarter on the total number of people placed in restrictive housing during that time period, disaggregated by race, age, gender identity, mental health treatment level and length of time in restrictive housing, and data on all disposition outcomes of all restrictive housing hearing during such time period, disaggregated by charge, race, age, gender identity and mental health treatment level.
obligations.deadline_text: Beginning July 31, 2024, and within 30 days of the end of each subsequent quarter
obligations.law_title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to banning solitary confinement in city jails and establishing standards for the use of restrictive housing and emergency lock-ins

obligations.action_summary: Refrain from placing incarcerated persons in restrictive housing for longer than necessary and for no more than a total of 60 days in any 12-month period.
obligations.quote: The department shall not place an incarcerated person in restrictive housing for longer than necessary and for no more than a total of 60 days in any 12 month period.
obligations.law_title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to banning solitary confinement in city jails and establishing standards for the use of restrictive housing and emergency lock-ins

obligations.action_summary: Conduct a meaningful review within 15 days of placement in restrictive housing to determine if the incarcerated person continues to present a specific, significant and imminent threat, and provide written reasons and any recommended program, treatment, service, or corrective action.
obligations.quote: Within 15 days of placement of an incarcerated person in restrictive housing, the department shall meaningfully review such placement to determine whether the incarcerated person continues to present a specific, significant and imminent threat to the safety and security of other persons if housed outside restrictive housing. If an individual is not discharged from restrictive housing after review, the department shall provide in writing to the incarcerated person: (i) the reasons for the determination that such person must remain in restrictive housing and (ii) any recommended program, treatment, service, or corrective action.
obligations.deadline_text: Within 15 days of placement of an incarcerated person in restrictive housing
obligations.law_title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to banning solitary confinement in city jails and establishing standards for the use of restrictive housing and emergency lock-ins

obligations.action_summary: Provide incarcerated persons in restrictive housing access to available programs, treatment and services.
obligations.quote: The department shall provide the incarcerated person access to such available programs, treatment and services.
obligations.law_title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to banning solitary confinement in city jails and establishing standards for the use of restrictive housing and emergency lock-ins

obligations.action_summary: Discharge an incarcerated person from restrictive housing if such person has not engaged in behavior presenting a specific, significant, and imminent threat during the preceding 15 days, and in all circumstances discharge within 30 days after initial placement.
obligations.quote: The department shall discharge an incarcerated person from restrictive housing if such person has not engaged in behavior that presents a specific, significant, and imminent threat to the safety and security of themselves or other persons during the preceding 15 days. In all circumstances, the department shall discharge an incarcerated person from restrictive housing within 30 days after their initial placement in such housing.
obligations.deadline_text: within 30 days after their initial placement in such housing
obligations.law_title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to banning solitary confinement in city jails and establishing standards for the use of restrictive housing and emergency lock-ins

obligations.action_summary: Provide persons in restrictive housing interaction with other people and access to at least seven hours per day of out-of-cell congregate programming or activities comparable to those housed outside restrictive housing.
obligations.quote: A person placed in restrictive housing must have interaction with other people and access to congregate programming and amenities comparable to those housed outside restrictive housing, including access to at least seven hours per day of out-of-cell congregate programming or activities with groups of people in a group setting all in the same shared space without physical barriers separating such people that is conducive to meaningful and regular social interaction.
obligations.law_title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to banning solitary confinement in city jails and establishing standards for the use of restrictive housing and emergency lock-ins

obligations.action_summary: Document in writing or by videotape any decision by a person in restrictive housing to voluntarily decline to participate in congregate programming.
obligations.quote: A decision to voluntarily decline to participate in congregate programming must be done in writing or by videotape.
obligations.law_title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to banning solitary confinement in city jails and establishing standards for the use of restrictive housing and emergency lock-ins

obligations.action_summary: Utilize programming addressing unique needs of those in restrictive housing and provide access to core educational programming comparable to general population programs.
obligations.quote: The department shall utilize programming that addresses the unique needs of those in restrictive housing. The department shall provide persons in restrictive housing with access to core educational and other programming comparable to core programs in the general population.
obligations.law_title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to banning solitary confinement in city jails and establishing standards for the use of restrictive housing and emergency lock-ins

obligations.action_summary: Provide persons in restrictive housing access to evidence-based therapeutic interventions and restorative justice programs aimed at addressing the conduct resulting in their placement, with programs being individualized, trauma-informed, including positive incentive behavior modification models, and following best practices for violence interruption.
obligations.quote: The department shall also provide persons in restrictive housing access to evidence-based therapeutic interventions and restorative justice programs aimed at addressing the conduct resulting in their placement in restrictive housing. Such programs shall be individualized and trauma-informed, include positive incentive behavior modification models, and follow best practices for violence interruption.
obligations.law_title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to banning solitary confinement in city jails and establishing standards for the use of restrictive housing and emergency lock-ins

obligations.action_summary: Train staff that routinely interact with incarcerated persons in de-escalation techniques, conflict resolution, use of force policy, and related topics to address unique needs of those in restrictive housing units.
obligations.quote: Staff that routinely interact with incarcerated persons must be trained in de-escalation techniques, conflict resolution, the use of force policy, and related topics to address the unique needs of those in restrictive housing units.
obligations.law_title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to banning solitary confinement in city jails and establishing standards for the use of restrictive housing and emergency lock-ins

obligations.action_summary: Use positive incentives to encourage good behavior in restrictive housing units and use disciplinary sanctions only as a last resort in response to behavior presenting serious and evident danger.
obligations.quote: The department shall use positive incentives to encourage good behavior in restrictive housing units and may use disciplinary sanctions only as a last resort in response to behavior presenting a serious and evident danger to oneself or others after other measures have not alleviated such behavior.
obligations.law_title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to banning solitary confinement in city jails and establishing standards for the use of restrictive housing and emergency lock-ins

obligations.action_summary: Ensure all housing for medical or mental health support, transgender or gender non-conforming persons, voluntary protective custody, and school attendance comply with specified subdivisions and requirements related to congregate programming and positive incentives.
obligations.quote: All housing for medical or mental health support provided to persons recommended to receive such support by the entity providing and,or overseeing correctional medical and mental health, including placement in contagious disease units, housing for people who are transgender or gender non-conforming, housing for voluntary protective custody, and housing for purposes of school attendance, shall comply with subdivisions (b), (c), (e), (i), (j) and (k) of this section and paragraphs 4, 5, and 6 of this subdivision.
obligations.law_title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to banning solitary confinement in city jails and establishing standards for the use of restrictive housing and emergency lock-ins

obligations.action_summary: For contagious disease units, allow persons to be held for as limited a time as medically necessary as exclusively determined by health care staff, in the least restrictive environment that is medically appropriate.
obligations.quote: For purposes of contagious disease units, after a referral from health care staff, a person may be held in a medical unit overseen by health care staff, for as limited a time as medically necessary as exclusively determined by health care staff, in the least restrictive environment that is medically appropriate.
obligations.law_title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to banning solitary confinement in city jails and establishing standards for the use of restrictive housing and emergency lock-ins

obligations.action_summary: Provide individuals in contagious disease units comparable access to phone calls, emails, visits, and programming as individuals incarcerated in the general population, done in a manner consistent with medical and mental health treatment being received.
obligations.quote: Individuals in a contagious disease unit must have comparable access as individuals incarcerated in the general population to phone calls, emails, visits, and programming done in a manner consistent with the medical and mental health treatment being received, such as at a physical distance determined appropriate by medical or mental health staff.Such access must be comparable to access provided to persons incarcerated outside of restrictive housing units.
obligations.law_title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to banning solitary confinement in city jails and establishing standards for the use of restrictive housing and emergency lock-ins

obligations.action_summary: Ensure all incarcerated persons have access to at least 14 out-of-cell hours every day except while in de-escalation confinement or during emergency lock-ins.
obligations.quote: All incarcerated persons must have access to at least 14 out-of-cell hours every day except while in de-escalation confinement pursuant to subdivision c of this section and during emergency lock-ins pursuant to subdivision j of this section.
obligations.law_title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to banning solitary confinement in city jails and establishing standards for the use of restrictive housing and emergency lock-ins

obligations.action_summary: Allow incarcerated persons to congregate with others and move about their housing area freely during out-of-cell time and have access to education and programming.
obligations.quote: Incarcerated persons may congregate with others and move about their housing area freely during out-of-cell time and have access to education and programming pursuant to section 9-110 of the administrative code.
obligations.law_title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to banning solitary confinement in city jails and establishing standards for the use of restrictive housing and emergency lock-ins

obligations.action_summary: Use emergency lock-ins only when the Commissioner or equivalent senior leadership determines such lock-in is necessary to de-escalate an emergency posing specific, significant and imminent harm, only when no less restrictive means are available, and only as a last resort after exhausting less restrictive measures.
obligations.quote: Emergency lock-ins may only be used when the Commissioner, a Deputy Commissioner, or another equivalent member of department senior leadership with responsibility for the operations of security for a facility determines that such lock-in is necessary to de-escalate an emergency that poses a threat of specific, significant and imminent harm to incarcerated persons or staff. Emergency lock-ins may only be used when there are no less restrictive means available to address an emergency circumstance and only as a last resort after exhausting less restrictive measures.
obligations.law_title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to banning solitary confinement in city jails and establishing standards for the use of restrictive housing and emergency lock-ins

obligations.action_summary: Confine emergency lock-ins to as narrow an area as possible and limited number of people as possible, and lift emergency lock-ins as quickly as possible.
obligations.quote: Emergency lock-ins must be confined to as narrow an area as possible and limited number of people as possible. The department shall lift emergency lock-ins as quickly as possible.
obligations.law_title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to banning solitary confinement in city jails and establishing standards for the use of restrictive housing and emergency lock-ins

obligations.action_summary: Have the Commissioner, Deputy Commissioner, or equivalent senior leadership review emergency lock-ins at least every hour.
obligations.quote: The Commissioner, a Deputy Commissioner, or another equivalent member of department senior leadership over the operations of security shall review such lock-ins at least every hour.
obligations.law_title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to banning solitary confinement in city jails and establishing standards for the use of restrictive housing and emergency lock-ins

obligations.action_summary: Limit emergency lock-ins to no more than four hours.
obligations.quote: Such lock-ins may not last more than four hours.
obligations.law_title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to banning solitary confinement in city jails and establishing standards for the use of restrictive housing and emergency lock-ins

obligations.action_summary: Conduct visual and aural observation of every person in emergency lock-in every 15 minutes, refer health concerns to medical or mental health staff, and bring persons needing medical treatment to the medical clinic.
obligations.quote: Throughout an emergency lock-in, the department shall conduct visual and aural observation of every person locked in every fifteen (15) minutes, shall refer any health concerns to medical or mental health staff, and shall bring any person displaying any indications of any need for medical documentation, observation, or treatment to the medical clinic.
obligations.law_title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to banning solitary confinement in city jails and establishing standards for the use of restrictive housing and emergency lock-ins

obligations.action_summary: Provide persons in emergency lock-in access to a tablet or other device allowing phone calls outside the facility and to medical staff in the facility, except in department-wide or facility emergency lock-ins.
obligations.quote: Throughout an emergency lock-in, other than in a department-wide emergency lock-in or a facility emergency lock-in, each person locked in shall have access to a tablet or other device that allows the person to make phone calls both outside of the facility and to medical staff in the facility.
obligations.law_title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to banning solitary confinement in city jails and establishing standards for the use of restrictive housing and emergency lock-ins

obligations.action_summary: Immediately provide public notice on the department's website of an emergency lock-in, including information on restrictions on visits, phone calls, counsel visits or court appearances.
obligations.quote: The department shall immediately provide notice to the public on its website of an emergency lock-in, including information on any restrictions on visits, phone calls, counsel visits or court appearances.
obligations.deadline_text: immediately
obligations.law_title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to banning solitary confinement in city jails and establishing standards for the use of restrictive housing and emergency lock-ins

obligations.action_summary: Prepare an incident report for each emergency lock-in including description of necessity, exhaustion of less restrictive measures, number of people held, length of lock-in, areas affected, health services affected, impact on visits and court appearances, programs affected, actions taken to resolve, and staff diverted.
obligations.quote: For each instance an emergency lock-in is imposed, the department shall prepare an incident report that includes: (a) A description of why the lock-in was necessary to investigate or de-escalate an emergency, including the ways in which it posed a threat of specific, significant and imminent harm; (b) A description of how other less restrictive measures were exhausted; (c) The number of people held in lock-in; (d) The length of lock-in; (e) The areas affected and the reasons such areas were subject to the emergency lock-in; (f) The medical and mental health services affected, the number of scheduled medical and or mental health appointments missed and requests that were denied; (g) Whether visits, counsel visits or court appearances were affected; (h) What programs, if any, were affected; (i) All actions taken during the lock-in to resolve and address the lock-in; and (j) The number of staff diverted for the lock-in.
obligations.law_title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to banning solitary confinement in city jails and establishing standards for the use of restrictive housing and emergency lock-ins

obligations.action_summary: Provide the speaker of the council and the board of correction all emergency lock-in incident reports for the preceding quarter and post such reports on the department's website with identifying information redacted.
obligations.quote: Beginning July 15, 2024, and within 15 days of the end of each subsequent quarter, the department shall provide the speaker of the council and the board of correction all such reports for the preceding quarter and shall post all such reports on the department's website with any identifying information redacted.
obligations.deadline_text: Beginning July 15, 2024, and within 15 days of the end of each subsequent quarter
obligations.law_title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to banning solitary confinement in city jails and establishing standards for the use of restrictive housing and emergency lock-ins

obligations.action_summary: Provide the speaker of the council and the board of correction a quarterly report on emergency lock-in data including total number of lock-ins, areas affected, length of each lock-in, and number of incarcerated people subject to each lock-in disaggregated by race, age, gender identity, mental health treatment level, and length of time in cell confinement.
obligations.quote: Beginning July 15, 2024, and within 15 days of the end of each subsequent quarter, the department shall provide to the speaker of the council and the board of correction a report on the total number of lock-ins occurring during the preceding quarter, the areas affected by each such lock-in, the length of each such lock-in and number of incarcerated people subject to each such lock-in, disaggregated by race, age, gender identity, mental health treatment level and length of time in cell confinement.
obligations.deadline_text: Beginning July 15, 2024, and within 15 days of the end of each subsequent quarter
obligations.law_title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to banning solitary confinement in city jails and establishing standards for the use of restrictive housing and emergency lock-ins

obligations.action_summary: Provide incarcerated persons under age 22 access to trauma-informed, age-appropriate programming and services on a consistent, regular basis.
obligations.quote: Incarcerated persons under the age of 22 shall receive access to trauma-informed, age-appropriate programming and services on a consistent, regular basis.
obligations.law_title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to banning solitary confinement in city jails and establishing standards for the use of restrictive housing and emergency lock-ins

obligations.action_summary: Take any actions necessary for the implementation of this local law, including the promulgation of rules relating to procedures and penalties necessary to effectuate this section.

obligations.quote: Each photo noise violation monitoring device shall undergo an annual calibration check by the manufacturer of such device or by the department. Subject to appropriations, the department shall ensure that there are no less than 5 photo noise monitoring devices in each borough by and after September 30, 2025.
